title: Entomo-virological surveillance of yellow fever, dengue, zika, and chikungunya viruses
author: Calderón-Peláez, Mantilla-Granados, et al.

steps.title: Extract viral RNA from samples
steps.instruction: Thaw mosquito samples on ice, transfer each individual into a tube containing 400 µL diethyl‑pyrocarbonate‑treated water (Sigma‑Aldrich, D5758) using a curved‑tip syringe needle; crush specimens with microcentrifuge‑tube pestles (USA Scientific, 1415‑5390); transfer the cleared supernatant to the viral RNA extraction tubes of the RTP® DNA/RNA Virus Mini kit (Stratec, 1,040,100,300) and process according to the manufacturer’s protocol, heating the tubes at 65 °C for 15 min then at 95 °C for 10 min, mixing lysates with the binding solution, loading onto the minicolumn, washing twice, and eluting RNA with the supplied buffer; quantify the eluate with a Nanodrop (Implen) and either use immediately as template for RT‑PCR or store at –80 °C.

steps.title: First‑round semi‑nested RT‑PCR
steps.instruction: Set up a one‑step RT‑PCR reaction using Luna® Universal One‑Step RT‑PCR kit (Thermo Fisher) with 0.2 µM outer primers (four primer pairs) and 100–400 ng of purified RNA (use 300 ng for low‑concentration samples such as segmented females); include a negative control with nuclease‑free water; for DENV, ZIKV and CHIKV use primers from Calvo et al., and for YFV use the study‑specific primers (Table 1). Run the thermal program: reverse transcription at 50 °C for 15 min, initial denaturation at 95 °C for 2 min, then 30 cycles of 95 °C for 30 s, annealing at 55 °C for 30 s, extension at 72 °C for 30 s, followed by a final extension at 72 °C for 5 min.

steps.title: Second‑round PCR amplification
steps.instruction: For each virus, prepare a separate PCR using 2 µL of the first‑round amplicon as template; DENV reactions contain five internal primers (one forward and four reverse, one per serotype), while CHIKV, ZIKV and YFV reactions use a single inner primer pair; run the program: initial denaturation at 95 °C for 5 min, then 25 cycles of 95 °C for 30 s, annealing at 60 °C for 30 s, extension at 72 °C for 30 s, and a final extension at 72 °C for 5 min.

steps.title: Agarose gel electrophoresis of second‑round products
steps.instruction: Separate the second‑round PCR products on a 2 % agarose gel run at 90 V for 45 min; stain the gel with ethidium bromide (Sigma‑Aldrich) for 10–20 min; visualize bands using a BioRad Gel Doc XR Plus imaging system; include positive controls (viral RNA from supernatants of c6/36 cells infected with each virus) and negative controls for each amplification round.

steps.title: Optional: increase template amount
steps.instruction: When processing segmented female samples (head/thorax and abdomen) that yield RNA concentrations of 50–80 ng/µL, use 300 ng of RNA as template in the first‑round RT‑PCR to improve sensitivity.

steps.title: Confirm YFV amplicons by sequencing
steps.instruction: Purify YFV‑specific second‑round amplicons, perform Sanger sequencing, and analyse the obtained sequences with BLAST® (NCBI) to confirm identity against reference YFV sequences.
